query: For as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys in the form of nanoscale thin films or lithographically patterned nanoribbons, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs their magnetocaloric response and hysteresis during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles, given that the notable response reported for bulk forms may not persist in a genuinely low-dimensional state and that heat-transfer rate limits cycle frequency? Specify one controlled intervention, predicted observations relative to the as-deposited baseline, applicable operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification result.

generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, rare-earth-free Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 high-entropy-alloy thin films and lithographically patterned nanoribbon arrays on substrates; ribbons were 500 µm long, 300 nm wide, and 35 nm thick with 1 or 2 µm spacing. The material was amorphous or extremely fine/disordered, with a single cubic-type short-range order, no long-range crystalline order or secondary phases, and a smooth surface (Rq ≈ 0.79 nm, Ra ≈ 0.63 nm).
generation.intervention: The study compared thin films and nanoribbon arrays with 1 and 2 µm spacing, applied cyclic longitudinal tensile strain of 0–1% and 0–2% to films on Kapton, and annealed 1 µm-spaced nanoribbons at 700 K in flowing Ar + 2% N2 at 10 K/min. Samples were fabricated by five-source magnetron co-sputtering after electron-beam lithography.
generation.conditions: Structural characterization used TEM/SAED and AFM before and after annealing. SQUID measurements were performed from 2–300 K under 1 kOe in ZFC/FC modes and with fields parallel or perpendicular to the ribbon axis; hysteresis loops were measured at 5 and 300 K. Magnetocaloric isotherms covered 5–200 K in fields up to 50 kOe, with entropy change calculated by the Maxwell relation. Strain was restricted to the elastic regime up to 2%; higher strain was avoided because of possible cracking.
generation.structural_mediator: Re addition refined the grains, increased lattice distortion and excess free volume, and produced several-nanometer-wide amorphous regions at grain boundaries. After irradiation, NbMoTaW showed larger He bubbles segregated and aligned along grain boundaries, whereas bubbles and grain-boundary segregation were not clearly discernible in NbMoTaWRe.
generation.mechanism: The additional grain boundaries, lattice distortion, excess volumes, and amorphous grain-boundary regions in NbMoTaWRe provide defect-sink sites that accelerate annihilation of irradiation-induced vacancies and related damage, suppressing He-bubble growth and segregation. In NbMoTaW, grain-boundary He-bubble accumulation promotes boundary embrittlement and irradiation hardening.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-deposited, unannealed state, 700 K annealing should enhance the magnetization and maximum conventional isothermal magnetic entropy change of 1 µm-spaced nanoribbons without bulk crystallization; elastic longitudinal strain should strengthen the magnetic response above 100 K without shifting the blocking peak or breaking film in-plane isotropy; increasing ribbon spacing to 2 µm should eliminate coupling-related in-plane anisotropy.
generation.baseline: As-deposited, unannealed and unstrained Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 films or nanoribbons measured under otherwise identical conditions. For the principal magnetocaloric comparison, the baseline was the as-deposited 1 µm-spaced nanoribbon array, with maximum −ΔSM ≈ 1.25 J kg−1 K−1 at 140 K and ΔH = 50 kOe.
generation.boundary: The annealing result applies to the metastable pre-crystallization state at 700 K; full conversion to a polycrystalline phase occurred only near 1000 K. Magnetocaloric enhancement was established for 1 µm-spaced ribbons, with an inverse effect below 20 K and a broad conventional response from about 40–200 K. Strain conclusions apply within the elastic 0–2% range. Magnetic decoupling and overlapping parallel/perpendicular low-temperature loops were observed at 2 µm ribbon spacing. The reported entropy-change magnitude remains modest relative to ordered bulk FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs.

falsification_experiment.design: The key tests were parallel-versus-perpendicular SQUID M(H) loops and ZFC/FC M(T) curves before and after strain or 700 K annealing, together with −ΔSM(T) derived from temperature-resolved magnetization isotherms up to 50 kOe. TEM/SAED, AFM, and temperature-dependent resistivity distinguished short-range relaxation at 700 K from crystallization near 1000 K.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
